pairs.evidence: src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:43 buildTriggerConfig fills a flat settings dictionary of leaf values (cron, url, watch_paths, conditions), one fixed branch per trigger type, so the file never describes a graph of live objects. Searches of the context directories for _requires_, _disabled_, instantiate, new Function and eval( found nothing, so none of the four object-graph obligations apply.

techniques.evidence: src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:46 Each trigger type has its own branch and a fixed set of keys. The technique's 'when not to use' clause excludes this case, and no loader directives are mixed with constructor arguments.
src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:80 Values are plain leaves (a URL string). No value can be read as a reference, so there is no sigil to define.

src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:122 Composite conditions are literal event_type strings matched at runtime, not config ids that resolve to instances. There is no resolver and no graph that could contain a cycle.

src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:89 Computed values come from TypeScript code in the form builder, not from expressions the config evaluates. No eval or new Function appears in the context.
src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:127 One form state produces one config. There is no base/override layering, so there are no repeated-key semantics to mark.
src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/configs/buildTriggerConfig.ts:39 The config is built in memory from form fields. There is no cross-file include and no relative id to expand.
